Due to the absence of fuel dispensing rates for LE, the same considerations presented for LNG are applied to LE; please refer Section 4.3.2.The same aircraft operating procedures mentioned for LNG in Section 4.3.2 are applicable to LE. 4.4 Cryogenic Fuels Market Analysis There are multiple market factors that influence fuel adoption. These include price (relative to conventional fuel), availability, compatibility, emissions, and policy factors. The availability of capital and federal loan guarantees to build and demonstrate first-of-a-kind aviation “fuel” plants will impact markets and the timeliness of deploying new fuels to the aviation market. Hydrogen, LNG, ethane, and other future aviation fuels will be heavily impacted by policies, as newly deployed fuels generally cost more than conventional fuels. 4.4.1 Cryogenic Hydrogen The development of a hydrogen market, whether cryogenic or not, will be dependent on factors such as technology advancement, infrastructure deployment, policy support, and cost- competitiveness. Each of these factors are interdependent and any changes in status will shift the trajectory of hydrogen demand. As an example of this interdependence, the U.S. DOE hydrogen roadmap lists possible U.S. hydrogen demand for different sectors by 2050 assuming hydrogen can be supplied at a threshold price (see Figure A-1 for more detail). For medium- and heavy- duty trucking, the threshold price is between $4/kg and $5/kg (DOE 2023a). If hydrogen cannot be delivered to medium- and heavy-duty trucks at the threshold price, hydrogen is not cost- competitive with the incumbent (e.g., diesel) and other alternative vehicle fuels (e.g., battery electric, biofuels) and hydrogen demand will not reach projected 2050 values of 5 MMT/yr to 8 MMT/yr (DOE 2023a). To avoid this scenario, some or all other factors (i.e., technology advancement, infrastructure deployment, policy favorability) must play a role such that the cost threshold can be met over time. In addition, if hydrogen price reduction over time is noticeable, it can spark further investment in technology development and deployment, as well as policy support, that can help the price reach parity with the incumbent. Notably, the U.S. DOE hydrogen roadmap does not include a specific callout to hydrogen demand for aviation (DOE 2023a).
